title: Drop the lowest score and stricter letter grades
prompt:
Change two rules of the grade book.

1. Dropping the lowest score. A student who has 4 or more recorded scores has the single lowest one dropped: it does not count anywhere (average, number of scores, letter grade, per-course averages, ranking and report all use only the scores that count). If several scores are equally low, the one recorded first is dropped. A student with fewer than 4 scores loses nothing. The drop is recomputed from all the recorded scores every time (a fifth score may change which one is dropped). The `(N scores)` and `(N)` counts show the number of scores that count.
2. Stricter letter grades. A is an average of 92 or more, B 84 or more, C 74 or more, D 62 or more, F anything lower (it used to be 90, 80, 70 and 60). As before the letter is decided from the exact average, not from the rounded one printed.

Everything else must behave as it does now.
